metadata.description: Expanded star catalog for Constellation Study App

stars.name: Sirius
stars.notes: Brightest star in the night sky. Binary system with a white dwarf companion.

stars.name: Canopus
stars.notes: Second brightest star. Used by spacecraft for navigation.

stars.name: Arcturus
stars.notes: Fourth brightest star. An orange giant, 25 times the Sun's radius.

stars.name: Vega
stars.notes: Fifth brightest star. Former North Star ~12,000 BC. Corner of Summer Triangle.

stars.name: Capella
stars.notes: Sixth brightest. Actually a quadruple star system of two binary pairs.

stars.name: Rigel
stars.notes: Seventh brightest. Blue supergiant ~120,000x Sun's luminosity.

stars.name: Procyon
stars.notes: Eighth brightest. One of the nearest stars with a white dwarf companion.

stars.name: Betelgeuse
stars.notes: Red supergiant ~700x Sun's diameter. May go supernova within 100,000 years.

stars.name: Altair
stars.notes: Spins once every 8.9 hours, causing visible oblateness. Corner of Summer Triangle.

stars.name: Aldebaran
stars.notes: The eye of the Bull. Orange giant 44x Sun's diameter. Not actually in the Hyades.

stars.name: Antares
stars.notes: Name means 'Rival of Mars' due to its red color. ~680x Sun's diameter.

stars.name: Pollux
stars.notes: Brightest star in Gemini. Has an exoplanet (Pollux b) confirmed in 2006.

stars.name: Fomalhaut
stars.notes: One of the first stars to have a directly imaged exoplanet (Fomalhaut b).

stars.name: Deneb
stars.notes: One of the most luminous stars known. Corner of Summer Triangle.

stars.name: Regulus
stars.notes: The Lion's Heart. Spins so fast it's significantly oblate. Quadruple star system.

stars.name: Castor
stars.notes: A spectacular sextuple star system — three pairs orbiting each other.

stars.name: Bellatrix
stars.notes: The Amazon Star. A blue giant ~630x Sun's luminosity.

stars.name: Shaula
stars.notes: The Stinger. A blue subgiant and triple star system.

stars.name: Alnilam
stars.notes: Center star of Orion's Belt. A blue supergiant, the most distant naked-eye star in Orion.

stars.name: Dubhe
stars.notes: Pointer star to Polaris. An orange giant in a triple system.

stars.name: Mirfak
stars.notes: Alpha Persei. A white supergiant, brightest star in Perseus.

stars.name: Wezen
stars.notes: A yellow-white supergiant, one of the most luminous stars visible.

stars.name: Alkaid
stars.notes: End of the Big Dipper's handle. Moving in a different direction from other Dipper stars.

stars.name: Sargas
stars.notes: Located in the Scorpion's tail. A bright giant star.

stars.name: Alhena
stars.notes: A white subgiant and the third brightest star in Gemini.

stars.name: Avior
stars.notes: A navigational star. An orange giant double star.

stars.name: Alphecca
stars.notes: Also called Gemma. The brightest star in the Northern Crown.

stars.name: Alpheratz
stars.notes: Shared with Pegasus (delta Peg). A mercury-manganese star.

stars.name: Mirach
stars.notes: A red giant. Used as a guide to find the Andromeda Galaxy (M31).

stars.name: Almach
stars.notes: A beautiful double star with gold and blue components.

stars.name: Schedar
stars.notes: Alpha Cassiopeiae. An orange giant with irregular variations.

stars.name: Denebola
stars.notes: The Lion's Tail. A young main-sequence star with a debris disk.

stars.name: Algieba
stars.notes: A beautiful double star — orange and yellow components visible in small telescopes.

stars.name: Algol
stars.notes: The Demon Star. Eclipsing binary that dims from mag 2.1 to 3.4 every 2.87 days.

stars.name: Alnitak
stars.notes: Easternmost star of Orion's Belt. A triple system near the Horsehead Nebula.

stars.name: Mintaka
stars.notes: Westernmost star of Orion's Belt. An eclipsing binary.

stars.name: Saiph
stars.notes: Marks one of Orion's knees. Despite being a blue supergiant, appears dimmer due to distance.

stars.name: Elnath
stars.notes: Also Beta Tauri. A blue giant shared with Auriga on the border.

stars.name: Adhara
stars.notes: An extremely luminous blue supergiant and strong UV source.

stars.name: Albireo
stars.notes: Famous double star: gold primary + blue companion. One of the finest doubles in the sky.

stars.name: Sadr
stars.notes: Center of the Northern Cross. A yellow-white supergiant.

stars.name: Gienah
stars.notes: Epsilon Cygni. An orange giant star.

stars.name: Tarazed
stars.notes: Gamma Aquilae. An orange giant, 2nd brightest in Aquila.

stars.name: Nunki
stars.notes: Sigma Sagittarii. One of the oldest known star names (Sumerian origin).

stars.name: Kaus Australis
stars.notes: Epsilon Sagittarii. Brightest star in Sagittarius, bottom of the Teapot.

stars.name: Spica
stars.notes: A close spectroscopic binary. The 'ear of wheat' held by Virgo.

stars.name: Izar
stars.notes: Epsilon Boötis. Beautiful double star: orange giant + blue companion.

stars.name: Muphrid
stars.notes: Eta Boötis. A subgiant slightly more evolved than the Sun.

stars.name: Markab
stars.notes: Alpha Pegasi. One corner of the Great Square of Pegasus.

stars.name: Scheat
stars.notes: Beta Pegasi. A red giant variable star. Another corner of the Great Square.

stars.name: Algenib
stars.notes: Gamma Pegasi. Third corner of the Great Square.

stars.name: Enif
stars.notes: Epsilon Pegasi. An orange supergiant, the 'Nose' of Pegasus.

stars.name: Porrima
stars.notes: Gamma Virginis. A beautiful binary that takes 169 years to orbit.

stars.name: Alpha Centauri
stars.notes: Nearest star system to the Sun. Triple system with Proxima Centauri at 4.24 ly.

stars.name: Hadar
stars.notes: Beta Centauri. A blue giant and the 11th brightest star in the sky.
